Naimiśi is the epithet of Śitibāhu aiṣakṛta in the Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa. It is probably to be taken as an indication that Śitibāhu came from the Naimiśa forest.
Foot notes i. 363 (Journal of the American Oriental Society, 26, 192).

Naimiśīya, Naimiṣīya denotes the dwellers in the Naimiśa forest. They are mentioned in the kāṭhaka Saṃhitā and the Brāhmaṇas, being clearly of special sanctity. Hence in the Epic the Mahābhārata is said to have been recited to the ṛṣis dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest.
Foot notes pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xxv. 6, 4; Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa, i. 363 (Journal of the American Oriental Society, 26, 192).
kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa, xxvi. 5; xxviii. 4; Chāndogya upaniṣad, i. 2, 13; Naimiṣya, kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, x. 6 (Indische Studien, 3, 469). The cerebrals seems to be universal later.
